questions.question: If “+” denotes “multiplied by”, “-” denotes “added to”, “×” denotes “divided by” and “÷” denotes “subtracted from”, then which of the following equation is true?

In the following question, by using which mathematical operators will the expression become correct?

35 ?5 ?10 ?15 ? 4
questions.solution:
Using BODMAS rule

Option 1:

35 ÷ 5 + 10 = 15 × 4

7 + 10 = 60

17 is not equal to 60

Option 2:

35 × 5 ÷ 10 > 15 × 4

35 × 1/2 > 60

17.5 is not greater than 60

Option 3:

**35 ÷ 5 × 10 > 15 × 4**

**7 × 10 > 60**

**70 > 60 is correct**

Option 4:

35 ÷ 5 × 10 < 15 + 4

7 × 10 < 15 + 4

70 < 17 is not true

Hence, option 3 is correct

questions.question: If 26 (52) 8 and 48 (192) 16, then what is the value of 'A' in A (175) 14?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is:

Logic: (First Number **× Last Number) ÷ 4 = Middle Number**

(26 × 8) ÷ 4 = 52

(48 × 16) ÷ 4 = 192

Similarly,

(A × 14) ÷ 4 = 175

A × 14 = 175 × 4 

A = (175 × 4) ÷ 14 

∴ A = 50

Hence, 50 is correct.

questions.question:
How many rectangles are there in the given figure?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dda29fc71c5ba5089b4a30be9dc4aee8c4e2839c09fdc8f579b0eeb8969f3ac2.png]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/LtGj6bPC3MU4pCFyLnXBpJVwZXVDMBz5wS3reWirRd7PjjRdlDLz-8Jk5zgwQryUyr9ar6_fLYm3XChgSRobFdSvoPg--RujRdwN-RyMXKU0RmHwghjTePQ0wqYiRe6hUJA_i3Ry] 

**__Formula used for equal number of rows and column:__**

Total number of rectangle ⇒ n³ + (n-1)³ + (n-2)³

n → number of rows/column

__Formula used for unequal number of rows and column:__

Total number of rectangle ⇒ (1 + 2 +......+ R) x (1 + 2 + .....+ C)

R → number of rows.

C → number of columns.

**In this problem, the number of rows and column are not equal.**

R → 3, C → 4

So, the number of rectangle in this figure = (1 + 2 +......+ R) x (1 + 2 + .....+ C) 

⇒ (1 + 2 + 3) x (1 + 2 + 3 + 4)

⇒ 6 x 10 = **60**

 [IMAGE: https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/zJZD7BEBrN9Ya0T0v4dpvMca5Wsxk8Ltg6-BUuvQeTk_5yz97OF41ZQbfJAHKq5PHc7e6afaJl7yuG7CPmRQCQqsTqQrTkn_0taBZWGLdwPgrB5YyfJrTzFcqbUEHrhJUh7tsExt]

questions.question:
In each of the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All grapes are green.

II. Some green are hard.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some green are grapes.

II. Some hard are grapes.

III. No grape is hard.
questions.solution:
By drawing Venn diagram:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ac892b24149c9f2c0d50fcb51430cc2aebdb1573036cf1d1e1e5b23e39b09aa.png] 

**Conclusion 1.** Some green are grapes → True (This is definitely true)

**Conclusion 2:** Some hard are grapes → False (This is possible but not definite)

**Conclusion 3:** No grape is hard → False (This is definitely False)

Hence, only Conclusion 1 follows.

questions.question:
Two position of a cube are shown below. What will come opposite to face containing ‘9’?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/83a462e917d6448c764d0a5e38708edf69b45490089e92dc0b73940f83a8d0e8.png]
questions.solution:
There are two positions of the same dice is given.

In both the positions 8 is same.

So, when one element is the same in both the dices then rotate it either clockwise or anti-clockwise to find the opposite faces.

Here, in 1st position rotate clockwise from 8 so we get:

⇒ 8 ⇔ 7 ⇔ 9

In position 2, rotate clockwise from 8, we get:

⇒ 8 ⇔ 6 ⇔ 4

So, 7 is opposite to 6 and 9 is opposite to 4.

Hence, 4 is opposite to 9.

questions.question: A word is represented by only one set of numbers as given in any one of the alternatives. The columns and rows of **Matrix-I **are numbered from 0 to 4 and that a **Matrix-II **are numbered from 5 to 9. A letter from these matrices can be represented first by its row and row and next by its column, for example, **‘E’** can be represented by 10, 22 etc., and **‘O’ **can be represented by 56, 78 etc. Similarly, you have to identify the set for the word **“HALT”.** Matrix-I 0 1 2 3 4 0 T E R A H 1 E

The representation for HALT is

H → 04, 12, 21, 33, 40

A → 03, 14, 20, 32, 41

L → 55, 68, 77, 86, 99

T → 00, 13, 24, 31, 42

HALT → 21, 41, 68, 13
